author: Travis Chinn
title: Clay County Heritage Center celebrates the County's 175th birthday with new display - NewsBreak
text:
By Travis Chinn ,
1 days ago
SPENCER, Iowa ( KCAU ) — Clay County, IA, is celebrating its 175th birthday this year. To help celebrate, the Clay County Heritage Center in Spencer has put together a display of the county's history.
On Wednesday, the Heritage Center held an open house to show off the new exhibit.
The exhibit includes all 12 towns in Clay County, including special displays on the Clay County Fair and a bank robbery in Everly committed by Bonnie and Clyde.
Each of the communities in Clay County have their own story to tell.
Story continues below
"Some of the unique things include the history of towns. As Spencer's 1931 fire that almost took out our downtown; of course we touch on the Clay County Fair, which puts us on the map, which is exciting for the Clay County Fair. Each of these towns has unique histories. There's a lot of interesting railroad history. Some of our towns have a connection to Native American history and things of that sort," said Susan Christensen, Interim Director of the Clay County Heritage Center.
The exhibit is free to visit and is scheduled to be up until August of 2027, but may stay open longer if it's needed.
